stem: A reused soilless medium has compacted over time and drains more slowly than when new. Which response best follows root-zone diagnostic logic?
choices: Increase irrigation frequency first because slower drainage usually indicates the medium is drying unevenly between events.
Strengthen the nutrient recipe because compaction commonly reduces nutrient concentration more than root-zone aeration.
Characterize the changed physical condition and moisture response before adjusting irrigation or nutrition.
Keep the current program unchanged until input EC shifts, because stable feed chemistry is the best indicator that the root zone remains comparable.
rationale: Compaction can reduce pore space and alter drainage/aeration. Measuring the changed root-zone behavior before changing multiple variables preserves diagnostic clarity.
